skip_reason: Inbound scheduling-change call on an already-booked move, not a new-business sales conversation. Aundrea Verdi opens with 'I have a move booked for this upcoming Tuesday' and the entire call is about shifting the arrival window on that existing job because her new apartment will not release keys until 3:00 PM. Amy pulls up the existing profile ('Okay, fine here scheduled for September 22nd Tuesday'), checks afternoon availability, and the call ends with the booking unchanged pending the customer's decision. There is no lead intake, no quote form, no pricing pitch, no estimate and no booking attempt — the job is already sold. The 85-point sales scorecard does not apply and this call should not count toward the sales grading average.
top_strength: Amy handled a stressed customer with real patience and solved the problem behind the request rather than just answering the question asked. When Aundrea hesitated, Amy gave her room instead of pushing: 'Take your time, I know it's a lot to process making a decision. No, really, take your time.' More importantly, when Aundrea concluded she was stuck either way — morning was too early, afternoon was the only slot, and she still could not get keys before 3:00 — Amy reframed the schedule rather than accepting the dead end: 'We can just let me go to your apartment closer to 2230 cause we're estimating like an hour and a half to load your items here at the current address. So, I would say closer to 2:00 start time or 2:30 even would, would still work.' She used the load time she already knew to build a start time that lands the crew at the new address right at the key handoff, and offered a call-ahead ETA on top of it. She also removed the pressure to decide on the spot — 'it's definitely not an inconvenience for us just let us know' — and closed with the weekday and weekend hours so Aundrea knew exactly when she could call back.
coaching_note: Not scored on the sales rubric — this is an ops/scheduling call. One coaching observation worth passing along anyway: Amy solved the problem verbally but left nothing behind to hold it. The move is Tuesday, Aundrea is calling on a Friday evening, the apartment complex will not confirm an earlier key release until Monday morning, and the decision now sits with a boyfriend who was not on the call. Amy's own summary was 'I'll leave it for the 8:30 for now' — which means the customer is carrying the entire follow-up burden into a weekend. The higher-value close is a note on the job plus a proactive Monday morning check-in from Einstein ('I'll make a note and reach out Monday morning to see where you landed'), so a two-hour window change on a Tuesday move does not depend on the customer remembering to call back. Worth also confirming in writing that the 2:00–2:30 arrival option exists, since that verbal workaround is the thing most likely to get lost between Friday and Monday.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and unhurried on a call where the customer was clearly flustered — Amy explicitly named the stress ('I know it's a lot to process making a decision'), granted the hold request without friction ('No, no worries. Take your time'), and reassured her the change was not a burden, and the customer's tone stayed positive through to a genuine 'Thank you so much.'
